facts.topic: Metabolic syndrome / fatty liver - Hyderabad IT employees
facts.claim: Cross-sectional study of 345 IT employees in Hyderabad (July 2023 - July 2024, Scientific Reports 2025;15:10124): MAFLD (fatty liver) in 290 (84.06%), metabolic syndrome in 118 (34.20%).
facts.source_title: Prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease among information technology employees in India (Scientific Reports, 2025)
facts.note: Also indexed at PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40128210. 363 employees visited the clinic; 345 analysed. University of Hyderabad study per press coverage (siasat.com).

facts.topic: Obesity / dyslipidaemia / blood sugar - Hyderabad IT employees
facts.claim: Same Hyderabad study (n=345, median age 38): 244 (70.72%) obese by BMI; 264 (76.52%) had high LDL cholesterol; 72 (20.87%) had elevated fasting blood glucose. No separate diabetes prevalence or overall dyslipidaemia rate reported in what the search returned.
facts.source_title: Scientific Reports 2025 - MAFLD among IT employees in India
facts.note: Figures came from search-result summaries of the paper (WebFetch unavailable); obesity likely uses Asian BMI cut-offs - verify in full text before quoting on a slide. Press: https://thesouthfirst.com/health/study-finds-84-percent-of-hyderabad-it-employees-have-fatty-liver/

facts.topic: Metabolic risk - South India corporate IT employees (earlier study)
facts.claim: An earlier South India study of corporate IT employees (cited in the Hyderabad paper) estimated metabolic syndrome at 29.87%, with 44.02% overweight, 16.85% obese, 3.86% diabetic and 64.93% with low HDL-C.
facts.source_title: Diets, Lifestyles and Metabolic Risk Factors among Corporate Information Technology (IT) Employees in South India
facts.value: MetS 29.87%; overweight 44.02%; obese 16.85%; diabetes 3.86%; low HDL 64.93%
facts.note: The search summary attributed these numbers to the Nature paper's discussion of prior work; the original study appears to be PMC10421222, but sample size and city were not confirmed. Verify before use.

facts.topic: Metabolic syndrome - Delhi NCR IT professionals
facts.claim: Cross-sectional study (2023-2024) of IT professionals attending preventive health check-ups in Delhi and NCR: metabolic syndrome in 162 participants (40.60%) by NCEP-ATP III criteria; 88 males (43.56%) and 74 females (37.56%).
facts.source_title: Proportion of metabolic syndrome and gender differences among information technology professionals undergoing preventive health check-up in Delhi and NCR (J Family Med Prim Care)
facts.note: Total sample size not stated in snippet; 162/40.6% implies about 399 (derived, not stated). PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42257130/

facts.claim: Study of 1,350 young IT employees (mean age 33): diabetes 2.5%, hypertension 13.5%, overweight or obesity 51.4%, low HDL cholesterol 70.1% (most common lipid abnormality); two or more risk factors clustered in 63.5%, rising with age.
facts.source_title: High prevalence of cardiometabolic risk factors in young employees of Information Technology industry (2016)
facts.value: n=1,350; DM 2.5%; HTN 13.5%; overweight/obese 51.4%; low HDL 70.1%; >=2 risk factors 63.5%
facts.note: City given as Pune by the search summary only; not independently confirmed from the abstract text.

facts.topic: Hypertension / diabetes / dyslipidaemia / obesity - IT and BPO employees
facts.claim: Single-centre study of about 1,000 IT and BPO employees: 22% newly diagnosed hypertension, 10% diabetes, 36% dyslipidaemia, 40% obesity.
facts.source_title: Health problems and stress in Information Technology and Business Process Outsourcing employees (J Pharm Bioallied Sci, 2015)
facts.note: Sample size 'about 1,000' per search summary; city not confirmed (possibly Chennai - unverified).

facts.topic: Prediabetes / diabetes - urban working professionals (not IT-only)
facts.claim: Workforce Health Index 2026: of 7,088 HbA1c results from corporate employees and covered family members in urban India, about 25.4% were in the prediabetes range and 13.3% in the diabetes range; elevated HbA1c roughly twice as common in people in their 30s (about 33%) as in their 20s.
facts.source_title: Workforce Health Index 2026: Blood Sugar, Stress and Vitamin D Risks Among India's Urban Working Professionals (MedBound Times)
facts.note: Industry/vendor report via secondary news source, not peer-reviewed; not IT-specific. No IT-specific prediabetes study found.

facts.topic: Vitamin B12 / D deficiency - company executives (Mumbai)
facts.claim: Study of 75 male senior company executives (Mumbai): 65% had vitamin B12 deficiency (<193 pg/ml) and 28% had vitamin D deficiency (<7.6 ng/ml).
facts.source_title: Incidence of vitamin B12/D3 deficiency among company executives (Indian Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine)
facts.value: n=75; B12 deficiency 65%; vitamin D deficiency 28%
facts.note: Office executives, not specifically IT; older study (about 2007). Mumbai location per search summary.

facts.claim: A single-centre observational study in Pune (April-July 2013) of IT professionals presenting for routine health check-up concluded vitamin B12 deficiency is prevalent among IT professionals despite high income and varied diets.
facts.source_title: Opportunistic Screening of Vitamin B12 Deficiency in IT Professionals Presenting for Routine Health Check-up (J Clin Diagn Res, 2015; DOI 10.7860/jcdr/2015/16191.6866)
facts.note: Overall deficiency percentage and sample size could not be retrieved; do not quote a number from this study without checking full text.

facts.topic: Vitamin D / B12 deficiency - Pune general population
facts.claim: Observational study around Pune: vitamin B12 deficiency 52.2% urban and 64.8% rural; vitamin D deficiency 34.3% urban and 13% rural.
facts.source_title: Prevalence of deficiencies of serum vitamin D3 and vitamin B12 among urban and rural population in and around Pune, India
facts.value: Urban B12 def 52.2%; urban vit D def 34.3%
facts.note: General population, not IT employees; sample size not captured.

facts.topic: Vitamin D deficiency - Indian healthcare professionals (comparator)
facts.claim: Among 2,119 medical and paramedical staff across 18 Indian cities, 79% were vitamin D deficient, 15% insufficient and only 6% sufficient.
facts.source_title: Widespread vitamin D deficiency among Indian health care professionals
facts.note: Indoor-working professionals comparator, not IT.

facts.topic: Vitamin B12 deficiency - urban professionals (vendor data)
facts.claim: Loop Health page reports clinical B12 deficiency (<200 pg/mL) in 32.2% of 1,399 urban professionals.
facts.source_title: Vitamin B12 - Loop Health Workforce Health Index
facts.note: Methodology unclear; vendor data, not peer-reviewed.

facts.claim: 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis: pooled prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal pain among Indian IT professionals 66% (95% CI 56-75%); lower back 55% (95% CI 46-63%); neck 50% (95% CI 41-58%).
facts.source_title: Common pain sites, prevalence and predictors of work-related musculoskeletal pain among Indian information technology professionals: a systematic review and meta-analysis
facts.value: Any MSK pain 66%; low back 55%; neck 50%
facts.note: Strongest single source for the deck; number of pooled studies/participants not captured.

facts.topic: Musculoskeletal pain - software professionals in MNCs (2024)
facts.claim: Cross-sectional study of software professionals in multinational companies (May-October 2024): lower back pain 66.7%, neck pain 56.9%.
facts.source_title: Exploring musculoskeletal disorders and ergonomic challenges among software professionals: A cross sectional study (J Family Med Prim Care, 2025)
facts.note: Sample size and city not captured.

facts.topic: Musculoskeletal pain incl. wrist - IT professionals India
facts.claim: An Indian study of IT professionals reported neck pain 64.9%, low back pain 56.5%, shoulder pain 42.1%, arm pain 34.5% and wrist pain 19.8%.
facts.source_title: Prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal disorders among IT professionals in India - a literature review (IJRMS)
facts.note: Search summary called it 'an older study' without clearly naming which source; attribution to this review is uncertain. Verify before use.

facts.claim: Cross-sectional study of software professionals: neck (29.56%) and lower back (22.89%) were the most common sites of work-related MSD in the past 12 months.
facts.source_title: A cross sectional study on work related musculoskeletal disorders among software professionals (IJCMPH)
facts.note: Sample size and city not captured; shows wide range across studies.

facts.topic: Burnout, effort-reward imbalance and poor sleep - software engineers
facts.claim: Raju, Nithiya & Tipandjan (J Educ Health Promot, 2022): 200 software engineers (mean age 29.3, 32% women); effort-reward imbalance 72%, burnout 60%, poor sleep quality 70%; 12% slept under 6 hours; women scored higher on all three.

facts.note: City not confirmed. Also at https://www.academia.edu/92526951/

facts.topic: HR industry - share of employers covering parents and check-ups (India)
facts.claim: Survey reported December 2023: 70% of companies offer health insurance to employees' families but only 25% extend it to parents; 57% offer discounted health check-ups; only 10% offer mental-wellbeing benefits; under 30% of employees participate in company wellbeing initiatives; median sum insured Rs 3 lakh; under 5% offer a comprehensive healthcare plan.

facts.note: Commissioning firm of the survey not captured; 'discounted check-ups' is not the same as employer-funded.

facts.topic: Regulation - mandatory annual health check-ups (OSH Code)
facts.claim: Under India's Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (labour codes effective 21 November 2025), employers must provide free annual health check-ups for workers above a specified age (commonly reported as 40).
facts.source_title: India's Health Checkup Mandate: What HRs Must Do Now (Loop Health)
facts.note: Sources disagree on the age threshold (some say it depends on state notification) and whether it applies to IT establishments; also see https://getvisitapp.com/blog/employee-wellness-programmes/new-ahc-law-2025-explained-impact-on-employee-wellness-programs/ . Verify against the gazette before putting on a slide.

facts.topic: ROI - annual health check-ups and hospitalisation

facts.note: Secondary news source for an industry report; useful ROI slide.

research.gaps: I used all 12 searches. WebFetch was unavailable, so every figure comes from search-result summaries and should be checked against the full papers before going on slides. Not found: (1) the headline vitamin B12 deficiency percentage and sample size of the Pune IT study (JCDR 2015, PMC4717757); (2) any vitamin D prevalence study specific to IT staff (only executive, healthcare-worker and general-population comparators); (3) any peer-reviewed prediabetes study specific to IT staff (only the vendor Workforce Health Index 2026); (4) a dedicated insomnia or stress prevalence study other than Raju et al. 2022 (n=200, city unknown); (5) the cities for the Pune 2016 (n=1,350), IT/BPO (n=about 1,000), MSK and burnout studies, which are unconfirmed; (6) the total sample size of the Delhi NCR study (about 399 is my own calculation); (7) any Nagpur-specific data, and whether Persistent's or Infosys's Nagpur campuses run on-site check-ups; (8) TCS, Wipro and other employers' check-up policies, which I did not search; (9) any current, official Infosys India policy on check-ups for parents or spouses (only HALE co-pay plus anonymous Glassdoor posts); (10) the exact OSH Code age threshold and whether it applies to IT offices. Nothing was found on breakfast or nutrition offerings at executive check-ups, and I did not search for it.

checks.claim: Hyderabad IT employees study (Scientific Reports 2025;15:10124): n=345, July 2023 to July 2024; MAFLD (fatty liver) in 290 (84.06%); metabolic syndrome in 118 (34.20%).
checks.reason: Search of the Nature paper and press coverage matches every figure. Researchers were from the University of Hyderabad and the Asian Institute of Gastroenterology. MAFLD was diagnosed by FibroScan (vibration-controlled transient elastography), and recruitment ran from July 2023 to July 2024. Press coverage (South First, Siasat, Hans India) reports the same headline numbers.

checks.claim: Same Hyderabad study: 244 (70.72%) obese; 264 (76.52%) high LDL cholesterol.
checks.reason: The search summary of the paper gives 244 (70.72%) obese and 264 (76.52%) high LDL-C. Press rounds obesity to about 71%. The exact LDL and BMI cut-offs were not seen, so say 'by the study's criteria' on a slide.

checks.claim: Same Hyderabad study: 72 (20.87%) had elevated fasting blood glucose; median age 38.
checks.reason: Neither the 20.87% FBG figure nor the median age of 38 came up in this re-check. Both still rest only on the first researcher's search summary.

checks.claim: Earlier South India corporate IT employee study: 44.02% overweight, 16.85% obese, 64.93% low HDL-C.
checks.reason: The study is 'Diets, Lifestyles and Metabolic Risk Factors among Corporate IT Employees in South India' (Nutrients 2023;15(15):3404, doi 10.3390/nu15153404, PMC10421222). Search results directly attribute 44.02% overweight and 16.85% obese to it, and give low HDL-C as 'about 65%', which fits 64.93%. Sample size and city were still not confirmed.

checks.claim: Same South India study: metabolic syndrome 29.87%; diabetes 3.86%.
checks.reason: No re-check result confirmed the 29.87% MetS or 3.86% diabetes figures. Leave them off slides unless checked against the full text.

checks.claim: Delhi NCR IT professionals at preventive health check-ups (2023-2024): metabolic syndrome 162 (40.60%) by NCEP-ATP III; males 88 (43.56%), females 74 (37.56%).
checks.reason: All three percentages and counts match. The exact study period was August 2023 to July 2024. Participants were aged 18-60, had worked in IT for at least a year, and were chosen by random systematic sampling of preventive check-up attendees. Journal: J Family Med Prim Care, DOI 10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_2296_25. Total sample size is still not stated; 'about 399' is a derived figure and should not be quoted. Separate corroboration: a 2026 study of white-collar private-sector employees in Delhi and Bengaluru (BMC/Springer, s12982-026-02195-4) found MetS in 40.51%.

checks.claim: Young IT employees (2016), city reported as Pune: n=1,350, mean age 33; diabetes 2.5%, hypertension 13.5%, overweight/obesity 51.4%, low HDL 70.1%; 2+ risk factors 63.5%, rising with age.
checks.reason: The city is now confirmed. The paper is Limaye, Kulkarni, Deokar & Kumaran, Indian J Occup Environ Med 2016;20(1):64-67 (PMC4922281). It used health-check records from two IT firms in Pune: 1,350 of 5,800 employees, mean age 33 ± 6, 78% men. All quoted percentages match, and prediabetes was 6.5%.

checks.claim: IT and BPO employees (J Pharm Bioallied Sci 2015): about 1,000 employees; 22% newly diagnosed hypertension, 10% diabetes, 36% dyslipidaemia, 40% obesity.
checks.reason: Not re-checked because of the search budget. The sample size and city were already marked unconfirmed by the original researcher.

checks.claim: Workforce Health Index 2026: of 7,088 HbA1c results, 25.4% prediabetes and 13.3% diabetes range; elevated HbA1c about twice as common in 30s (about 33%) as in 20s.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. This is vendor data (Loop Health) reported by a secondary news site, not peer-reviewed and not IT-specific. If used, label it 'vendor data'.

checks.claim: 75 male senior company executives (Mumbai, about 2007): 65% vitamin B12 deficient, 28% vitamin D deficient.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. The study is old and covers office executives, not IT staff, and the Mumbai location is unconfirmed.

checks.claim: Pune IT professionals B12 study (JCDR 2015): vitamin B12 deficiency prevalent among IT professionals.
checks.reason: Not re-checked, and no headline percentage or sample size was ever retrieved. Do not quote a number from it.

checks.claim: Pune general population: B12 deficiency 52.2% urban / 64.8% rural; vitamin D deficiency 34.3% urban / 13% rural.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. This is general-population data, not IT employees, and the sample size was not captured.

checks.claim: 2,119 Indian medical/paramedical staff across 18 cities: 79% vitamin D deficient, 15% insufficient, 6% sufficient.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. It is a comparator group, not IT staff.

checks.claim: Loop Health: clinical B12 deficiency (<200 pg/mL) in 32.2% of 1,399 urban professionals.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. Vendor data with unclear methodology, already marked unconfirmed.

checks.claim: 2025 meta-analysis: pooled prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal pain among Indian IT professionals 66% (95% CI 56-75%).
checks.reason: Confirmed: 20 studies with a combined sample of 15,709 (from 707 screened). Pooled prevalence was 66% (95% CI 56-75), with very high heterogeneity (I² = 99.16%), and the authors urge caution. 'About two in three IT professionals' is a fair slide phrasing.

checks.claim: Same 2025 meta-analysis: lower back pain 55% (95% CI 46-63%); neck pain 50% (95% CI 41-58%).
checks.reason: The site-specific pooled figures did not appear in the retrieved abstract text, which only notes variation across body sites. Do not mix this up with a different 2024 meta-analysis of all Indian occupational workers (J Occup Health 2025;67(1):uiae077, PubMed 39688540), which reported 76% overall, 60% low back and 40% neck.

checks.claim: Software professionals in MNCs (May-Oct 2024, JFMPC 2025): lower back pain 66.7%, neck pain 56.9%.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. Sample size and city were not captured.

checks.claim: Indian IT professionals: neck 64.9%, low back 56.5%, shoulder 42.1%, arm 34.5%, wrist 19.8% (attributed to IJRMS literature review).
checks.reason: Not re-checked. The original researcher already flagged the attribution as uncertain, so do not use it.

checks.claim: Software professionals (IJCMPH): neck 29.56% and lower back 22.89% most common 12-month WMSD sites.
checks.reason: Not re-checked. Sample size and city not captured.

checks.claim: Raju et al. 2022 (J Educ Health Promot): 200 software engineers; effort-reward imbalance 72%, burnout 60%, poor sleep 70%, 12% under 6 h sleep.
checks.reason: Not re-checked because of the search budget. City unconfirmed.

checks.reason: Not re-checked in this pass. It rests on an official Infosys page, so the risk is low, but the page should be opened before quoting. Nothing found says whether HALE runs at the Nagpur campus.

checks.reason: Not re-checked. These are anonymous, old posts and should not go on a pitch slide.

checks.reason: Not re-checked in this pass. Official PDF, so the risk is low. Nagpur site coverage is still unknown.

checks.reason: Not re-checked in this pass. Official page, so the risk is low. Current limits not captured.

checks.claim: Survey reported December 2023: 70% of companies cover employees' families, only 25% cover parents; median sum insured Rs 3 lakh; under 5% offer comprehensive healthcare plan; under 30% employee participation in wellbeing initiatives.
checks.reason: The figures are confirmed (70% family, 25% parents, Rs 3 lakh median, under 5% comprehensive, under 30% participation). The missing source is Plum's 'Health Report of Corporate India 2023'. The Business Standard URL code (123112100500) points to 21 November 2023, not December. That date is inferred from the URL pattern, not read from the article.
checks.corrected_value: Source: Plum, Health Report of Corporate India 2023, via Business Standard, about 21 Nov 2023 (date inferred from URL).

checks.claim: Same 2023 survey: 57% of companies offer discounted health check-ups; only 10% offer mental-wellbeing benefits.
checks.reason: The re-check search returned nothing supporting the 57% or 10% figures. Check them against the full Plum report (plumhq.com/corporate-health-report-2023) before use.

checks.claim: Plum report (BusinessToday, 7 Oct 2026): median health-benefit spend per employee up 14.7% CAGR over three years; employers offering more than Rs 5 lakh cover up 53% since FY22.
checks.reason: Not re-checked because of the search budget. It is a vendor report covered by news.

checks.claim: OSH Code (labour codes effective 21 Nov 2025): employers must provide free annual health check-ups for workers above about 40.
checks.reason: Many HR-vendor and law-firm sources report the 40+ age threshold and the 21 Nov 2025 date. Whether it applies to IT is disputed. One source reports that Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya told Parliament (12 Feb 2026) that check-ups will be required for all workers aged 40+. Another guide says the OSH (Central) Rules 2026 (reportedly notified 8 May 2026) limit the free annual exam to notified high-risk sectors, so IT/services staff are not yet covered nationally, though state rules may apply. The gazette text was not checked. Suggested slide wording: 'The new labour codes push employers towards annual check-ups for staff aged 40+'. Do not claim it is mandatory for IT firms.

checks.claim: CII-MediBuddy study of 10,551 employees: 2.41% hospitalisation rate with three annual check-ups vs 7.27% with none (about threefold).
checks.reason: Several outlets confirm this; the source is the third edition of the CII-MediBuddy Workplace Health Report (ANI coverage around 2 Aug 2026, per its URL). Other findings: about 25% of employees skipped every annual check-up but made up 46% of inpatient claims and 43% of insurance payouts, and 52% do not act on check-up findings. These are associations from a sponsor-linked corporate dataset, not proof that check-ups cause the difference. Phrase it as 'associated with'.

research.gaps: I used all 12 WebSearch calls. WebFetch was not available, so every finding rests on search snippets. No current (2025-26) Nagpur headcount was found for any company: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Persistent, Tech Mahindra or Hexaware. The figures above are design capacities, announced targets, or old indicative numbers. Persistent's Nagpur start year (2004) comes from a secondary history page, and a directory gives 2007. Persistent's own site puts it only in IT Park MIDC Parsodi, not MIHAN. The formal inauguration date for TCS MIHAN was not confirmed; it was announced in 2011 and the architect lists it as completed in 2018. Opening dates were not found for Tech Mahindra or Hexaware in MIHAN. I found no 2025-26 news on Infosys Phase 2. I did not check whether 'IT Park Parsodi' and 'Gayatri Nagar IT Park' are the same place; they are commonly treated as one, but no source here confirms it. I also did not cover STPI Nagpur or other possible Nagpur employers such as Wipro, LTIMindtree, Capgemini, Atos, Zensar or Mphasis. The Ebix and GlobalLogic locations rest only on directory or listicle sources. For anything that goes on a pitch slide, check headcounts and addresses against company annual reports, MADC (mihansez.org) or local press before using them.

checks.claim: Infosys inaugurated its new development center in MIHAN SEZ, Nagpur, on 16 December 2023. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis performed the inauguration.
checks.reason: Infosys's own press release is dated 16 Dec 2023. Business Standard (article ID 123121600852, also 16 Dec 2023) reports the inauguration by Gadkari and Fadnavis at MIHAN-SEZ.

checks.claim: Infosys put more than INR 230 crore into a 265,000 sq ft building that can hold more than 3,000 employees under its hybrid workplace model.
checks.reason: The Infosys press release, BW Businessworld and IndianWeb2 all give INR 230+ crore, 265,000 sq ft and capacity for more than 3,000 employees under the hybrid model. On a slide, call this design capacity, not headcount. The campus also has low-energy cooling, rainwater harvesting and 100% wastewater recycling.

checks.claim: The center handles cloud, AI and digital work for clients in banking, retail, automobile and manufacturing.
checks.reason: Confirmed, but the claim lists only some of the industries. The press release names cloud, AI and digital work for telecommunications, banking, retail, aerospace, automobile, logistics and manufacturing.

checks.claim: ArchDaily: Infosys Nagpur Phase 1 holds 2,000+ employees on 33 of 142 acres, is IGBC Platinum certified and was completed in January 2023.
checks.reason: Not re-checked within the search budget, so it rests on one secondary architecture source. Its 2,000 figure also conflicts with Infosys's own 3,000+ capacity. For the deck, use the Infosys press release figures.

checks.claim: Infosys MIHAN 142-acre site will be built in three phases, with a total employment target of 50,000 (social media post).
checks.reason: The only source is a user-generated X post. No official source was found. Do not quote it on a slide.

checks.claim: Persistent's two Nagpur sites are both in IT Park, MIDC Parsodi: Gargi-Maitreyi (Plot No. 8 and 9) and the 2nd and 3rd floors of Infotech Tower, Nagpur 440022.
checks.reason: Persistent's company-overview page lists Gargi-Maitreyi, Plot 8 and 9, IT Park, MIDC Parsodi, Nagpur 440022. Persistent's LinkedIn page lists the 2nd and 3rd floors of Infotech Tower, IT Park, MIDC Parsodi. Persistent is in IT Park Parsodi, not MIHAN.

checks.claim: Persistent's Nagpur development center became operational in 2004.
checks.reason: The only source is the old (about 9-year-old) Goodreturns company-history page. A Glassdoor caption mentions '20 years in Nagpur' but gives no date. No Persistent press release or annual report confirmed the year. If used, write 'for about two decades', not '2004'.

checks.claim: No published Nagpur headcount for Persistent. Glassdoor rates Persistent Nagpur 4.2/5 from 553 reviews.
checks.reason: The Glassdoor location page appeared in search results, but the snippets did not show the 4.2 rating or the 553 review count, and these numbers change over time. That no published Nagpur headcount exists is consistent with what I found.

checks.claim: Persistent was founded in 1990, is headquartered in Pune, and had 23,941 employees in December 2024.
checks.reason: The 23,941 figure is out of date. Persistent's Q2 FY26 earnings call reported 26,224 employees at the end of Sept 2025, up from 25,314 at the end of Q1 FY26. Its Q3 FY26 press release boilerplate says 'over 26,500 employees in 18 countries'. Revelio Labs, a third party, estimates about 27,069 for March 2026. All are company-wide figures. Founding year and HQ were not re-checked.
checks.corrected_value: 26,224 employees at end of Q2 FY26 (Sept 2025, company-reported); 'over 26,500 employees in 18 countries' per Q3 FY26 release

checks.claim: TCS announced its Nagpur campus on 19 December 2011. CM Prithviraj Chavan laid the foundation stone for Phase I (Rs 600 crore) on a 54-acre MIHAN SEZ plot. The plan was for 16,000 associates once both phases were complete.
checks.reason: The TCS press release, Business Standard (published 20 Dec 2011) and domain-b confirm Rs 600 crore for Phase I, 54 acres in MIHAN SEZ, Chavan laying the foundation stone, and 16,000 planned capacity (Phase I has 8,200 seats). The snippets did not show the exact day of 19 Dec, but the date fits the coverage. 'December 2011' is safe to use. 16,000 is a 2011 plan, not current headcount.

checks.claim: The architect lists the TCS MIHAN campus as completed in 2018.

checks.claim: An RTI reply from MADC showed 24 companies operating in MIHAN SEZ, including HCL, TCS and Infosys, with 1,16,435 jobs: 78,771 in the SEZ and 37,664 outside it.
checks.reason: Nagpur Today (about 337 days old, so roughly Nov 2025; RTI filed by Abhay Kolarkar) gives 78,771 SEZ jobs, 37,664 non-SEZ jobs and 24 operating SEZ companies. Mahabharti gives the same count and adds 28 non-SEZ companies. A later Nagpur Today fact-check, however, says about 30 units are operating in the SEZ and puts total employment at 1.1 to 1.2 lakh. On a slide, write 'about 1.16 lakh jobs (RTI, late 2025)' and note that the count covers all sectors, not just IT.

checks.claim: After four new approvals in February 2025, the number of companies in MIHAN SEZ reached 50.
checks.reason: The Live Nagpur and Nagpur Updates both report this. The approvals came from the Unit Approval Committee meeting on 28 Jan 2025 and were reported on 12 Feb 2025. The four firms are Perla IT, Cloud Science Labs, People Global Services and Master Medical Solutions, together worth about Rs 4.5 crore and about 170 jobs. The 50 counts approved units, not operating ones, so it does not conflict with the RTI's 24 or the fact-check's ~30 operating units.
